title: How Statistics Can Be Misleading — Mark Liddell
skills: identify ways statistics can be presented misleadingly
evaluate graphs, percentages, averages, and data claims critically
recognize how framing and selective data can distort interpretation
assess quantitative evidence before accepting an argument or conclusion
alignment_note: Explains how statistics can be framed or presented in ways that create misleading impressions. Supports critical reading, quantitative literacy, source evaluation, argument analysis, and responsible interpretation of data-based claims across high school English and interdisciplinary research contexts.
